Grade each side by its ROLE; neither reading is presumed.

Name people and things only in the KJV's own words or in plain English; no titles, honorifics or capitalised epithets the text does not use (it says 'the child', not 'the Boy'); every Greek or Hebrew word you use is followed by its plain English meaning.

RETURN STRICT JSON AND NOTHING ELSE. No prose before or after it. No code fences.
{
  "verdict_tag": "HELD" | "PARTIAL" | "BROKEN",
  "defense_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "challenge_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "challenger_conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "counted_premises_defender": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE DEFENDER) you counted in conceded_links; [] when none
  "counted_premises_challenger": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE CHALLENGER) you counted in challenger_conceded_links; [] when none
  "reasoning": string -- the worked grading: the RESULT line, the CLAUSE line, KEYSTONE, both standings with their justification, both conceded-link itemizations, COLLISION POINTS, the citation check, OUT-OF-ROUND CONCESSIONS, DEFENDER CHAIN MARK and CHALLENGER CHAIN MARK, in the forms the rulebook below gives, one per line (newlines escaped as \n inside the JSON string)
}

THESE TOKENS ARE EXACT AND THE SETS ARE CLOSED. A value outside them is a FAILED judgment, not a nuance, and it will be counted as unreadable. Do NOT return "UNKNOWN" and do NOT invent a fourth tag: an UNKNOWN tag is scored as unclean AND is invisible to the unrecognised-tag report, so it is the one answer that hides itself.

verdict_tag MUST be the verdict word the VERDICT DEFINITIONS below give (first match wins). defense_standing, challenge_standing, conceded_links and challenger_conceded_links MUST equal the values your reasoning reaches under the rulebook; each counted_premises array MUST list exactly the premises its count counts.

THE RULEBOOK

JUDGE LAYER RULES:
[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. FORCED LINK (ruling 411): a link that the meaning of a pressed witness will not fit is graded BROKEN as a forced link even when the holding side answered that witness, if its answer does not show the fit. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the answer's own words that fail to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round: its reading, not only the words of a verse it quotes>" -- CARRIED BY: "<the words of the pressed witness's own verse that state its MEANS sentence, quoted from the KJV>" -- GROUND: [L1] <reference> "<the KJV words the answer cannot agree with>" | [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>, <gloss>), when the break turns on a word's meaning | [L3] <reference> "<KJV words>", for any cross-reference relied on (Commitment 13). Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. CARRIED BY shows that the pressed verse itself carries the MEANS sentence; K-FC, a TRIAL check, finds its words in that verse as the KJV reads it. A MEANS its own verse does not carry is no ground for a forced link. FAILS names what in the answer fails, its own reading; a verse does not fail. K-FF, a TRIAL check, returns for cure a FAILS that is only the words of a verse the answer quotes. PROVEN PRESS (md_notes_rulings 398 and 399: a press carries its layers; a press may carry its proof by reference to the round where the same layers were exhibited). A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). A proven press (md_notes_rulings 398) that the broken side's later rounds left UNANSWERED is also a BROKEN ground (COUNTING RULE; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground). Grade UNDERDETERMINED only when the witnesses and the answers, read together, still leave the point open; an answer that names a witness without showing a fit does not leave the point open (md_notes_rulings 419). k is the number of lines graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN. A side with any link graded BROKEN here cannot be SELF-SUPPORTED.

DEBATE RULE VIOLATION (Isaiah 28:10: "here a little, [and] there a little"). The rule on a BROKEN ground binds you as it binds the debaters. On every COLLISION POINTS line you grade DEFENDER LINK BROKEN or CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN, exhibit on that line itself at least two lower layers of DIFFERENT kinds, read by FOOTING LAYERS (md_notes_rulings 400). FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. A BROKEN line without them is a DEBATE RULE VIOLATION. The system checks every BROKEN line after you answer; a violating line is returned to you to cure, by exhibiting the two layers, or to answer in writing why it stands. An answer that does not exhibit them leaves the violation standing, and your judgment is then not counted. The same holds when your CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS count is 0 while you grade a link of that side BROKEN for a pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered. Both sides alike.

The standard reading of the Holy Scriptures affirms that Christ was conceived in the womb of the virgin Mary by the Holy Ghost without the agency of a human father, and therefore did not have a biological father.

### I. The Conception Occurred Before Joseph and Mary Came Together

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The Greek temporal prepositional phrase translated "before they came together" contains πρίν (*prin*, G4250, "before, formerly") and συνελθεῖν (*synelthein*, aorist active infinitive of συνέρχομαι, *synerchomai*, G4905, "to come together, to come together in cohabitation or conjugal union").
[L3] Matthew 1:25 confirms the absence of sexual intercourse until after the delivery: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." Here "knew" renders ἔγινωσκεν (*eginōsken*, imperfect active of γινώσκω, *ginōskō*, G1097, used of carnal knowledge, as in Genesis 4:1).
[L4] Because Mary was already found with child prior to any conjugal union (*synelthein*) with Joseph, and Joseph "knew her not" until after the birth, Joseph was not the physical or biological generator of the child.

---

### II. Mary's Explicit Testimony of Carnal Inexperience

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] The Greek present active indicative verb γινώσκω (*ginōskō*, G1097, "to know, understand, perceive, have carnal relations with") is paired with the negative particle οὐ (*ou*, G3756, absolute negation) and ἄνδρα (*andra*, accusative singular of ἀνήρ, *anēr*, G435, "a male person, a husband, a man").
[L3] Genesis 19:8 exhibits the exact semantic force of knowing a man as sexual relations: "Behold now, I have two daughters which have not known man."
[L4] Mary’s question establishes that at the time of the annunciation, she had no sexual relations with any male human being; therefore, the conception foretold could not proceed from human biological paternity.

### III. The Agency of Conception is the Holy Ghost and Divine Power

[L1] Luke 1:35: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] The Greek verb ἐπισκιάσει (*episkiasei*, future active indicative of ἐπισκιάζω, *episkiazō*, G1982) means "to overshadow, to cast a shade upon, to envelop in divine presence."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Greek phrase translated "is conceived" is τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν (*to gar en autē gennēthen*, aorist passive participle of γεννάω, *gennaō*, G1080, "to beget, to bear, to bring forth"), modified by the prepositional phrase ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου (*ek pneumatos estin hagiou*, "is of the Holy Ghost").
[L4] The origin and conception of the holy child was wrought by the divine overshadowing of the Holy Ghost (*ek pneumatos hagiou*), operating upon the womb of Mary, entirely replacing and excluding the biological seed or agency of a human male.

---

### IV. The Fulfillment of the Prophecy of the Virgin Birth

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] The Hebrew noun translated "virgin" is עַלְמָה (*‘almāh*, H5959, "a virgin, a young maiden of marriageable age who is unmarried and sexually untouched").
[L3] Matthew 1:22-23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." In Matthew 1:23, the text employs the Greek noun ἡ παρθένος (*hē parthenos*, G3933, "the virgin"), an explicit technical designation for an unmarried woman who has preserved her chastity.
[L4] Prophecy required that the mother conceive while retaining the status of a virgin (*parthenos*); a conception occurring through the natural biological agency of a human male would extinguish that status and falsify the divine sign.

---

### V. Legal Paternity Versus Biological Origin in the Genealogies

[L1] Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli."
[L2] The Greek parenthetical participle phrase ὢν ὡς ἐνομίζετο (*ōn hōs enomizeto*) employs ἐνομίζετο (imperfect passive of νομίζω, *nomizō*, G3543, "to hold by custom, to deem, to reckon, to suppose according to custom or law").
[L3] Matthew 1:16 departs from the generational formula "A begat B" used in the preceding fifteen verses: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." In Matthew 1:16, the relative pronoun "of whom" is feminine singular in the Greek: ἐξ ἧς (*ex hēs*), referring exclusively to Mary, whereas every prior generation in the genealogy from verses 2 to 16 uses the active verb ἐγέννησεν (*egennēsen*, "begat") applied to the male ancestor.
[L4] While Joseph was the customary and legal father according to the civic registers (*hōs enomizeto*), the scripture deliberately breaks the male begetting formula (*egennēsen*) at Joseph, attributing the birth exclusively to Mary (*ex hēs*), confirming that Joseph was not Christ's biological progenitor.

---

### DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew 1:18 exhibits that Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost before coming together (G4905, *synelthein*) with Joseph, and Matthew 1:25 exhibits that Joseph knew her not (G1097, *ginōskō*) till she brought forth her firstborn son.
2. Luke 1:34 exhibits that Mary had no carnal knowledge of a man (G1097, *ginōskō*), supported by Genesis 19:8 establishing that knowing a man signifies sexual relations.
3. Luke 1:35 and Matthew 1:20 exhibit that the conception was directly effected by the overshadowing (G1982, *episkiazō*) of the Holy Ghost, and generated of the Holy Ghost (G1080, *gennaō*).
4. Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23 exhibit that Christ was conceived by an untouched virgin (H5959, *‘almāh*; G3933, *parthenos*) without the natural biological seed of a man.
5. Luke 3:23 and Matthew 1:16 exhibit that Joseph was the father only by custom and legal reckoning (G3543, *nomizō*), with the genealogy attributing physical birth solely to the mother (feminine relative pronoun *ex hēs*).
6. Christ did not have a biological father.

The Son is sent forth from God, takes human flesh entirely from the woman, and is placed under the law through His birth into the covenant people and legal adoption into Joseph's Davidic house, fully fulfilling the law without a biological earthly father.

The challenger asserts under C4 that Luke 2:49 does not overturn Joseph's paternity because it refers to mission rather than physical loins. By subordinating the earthly parental claim to His divine origin and work, Christ Himself affirms that His true Father is God, consistent with Luke 1:35 where the child born of Mary is called "the Son of God" because He was conceived of the Holy Ghost [L3].

---

### CONCLUSION

The KJV text demonstrates with absolute precision that Jesus Christ did not have a biological father:
1. Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost prior to any physical union with Joseph (Matthew 1:18).
2. Mary herself attested that she knew not a man (Luke 1:34).
3. The conception was directly effected by the Holy Ghost overshadowing her (Luke 1:35, Matthew 1:20).
4. Isaiah's prophecy of the virginal conception was strictly fulfilled in this miraculous birth (Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:22-23).
5. Joseph maintained complete sexual abstinence toward Mary until after the birth took place (Matthew 1:25).
6. Joseph's relation to Jesus was strictly legal and social ("as was supposed", Luke 3:23), while physical begetting is attributed exclusively to Mary ("of whom was born Jesus", Matthew 1:16).

Therefore, the standard reading is fully sustained: Christ did not have a biological father.

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. An opening grant ("I grant it") followed by a layer that shows how the verse fits the answering side's case MEETS. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not. A charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never VOID for its words (ruling 421).
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. A LINK BROKEN line given with THE SAME JUDGE'S FORCED LINE on that collision is read with it as one ruling: the words that FORCED line quotes (its MEANS and its ANSWER) are the quotes of the break, so do not DISAGREE because the LINK BROKEN line itself quotes no answer words; judge the break by those quoted words, under the rest of this rule (pkgECP, either side alike). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and a rival reading of a contested word is not a break when the answer quotes the row words that carry it (CARRIED BY: a verse the answering round cites, at least 6 words in a row); layers named without such words do not carry a rival reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; pkgECW; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. Its cure line is PRESSED: D<n> vs C<m> | [<round>] | <the pressing words in quotation marks>, the round [DR1] or [DR2] against the defender, [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3] against the challenger, its words standing word for word in that round; it does not cure when a later round of the side that holds the link names every pressed witness the line rests on. A FORCED line breaks a link by meaning only when its MEANS quotes the pressing side's own sentence in the round it names; a verse re-quoted as the MEANS is not that, and when the item carries a CODE CHECK saying so, DISAGREE (pkgEFG, either side alike). When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. THE FOOTING RULE (pkgECB, ASK 267; either side alike): a LINK BROKEN line whose ground is that the link's step has no footing, or that its footing is borrowed from its own side's contested links, is not a break by meaning, and the meaning test above does not decide it: that the answer's words can agree with the meaning pressed does not answer a missing footing. On such a line a fit that rests on the very step the line says has no footing, or on the answering side's own contested links, is not a fit. AGREE when the answering side's rounds give that step no footing but its own contested links; DISAGREE when you quote the answering side's own words, in the round that gives them, footing the step on rows that are not its own contested links. Footing is the side's own rows and chain, not one verse that states the step (DG-61): a line that only says no verse states the step rests on an absence. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds. An answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, its layers included (THE ANSWER IN FULL, when given under an ANSWER CHECK line); an opening grant followed by a layer that shows the fit is not a bare grant. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. An opening grant ("I grant it") followed by a layer that shows how the verse fits the answering side's case MEETS. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not. A charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never VOID for its words (ruling 421).
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. A LINK BROKEN line given with THE SAME JUDGE'S FORCED LINE on that collision is read with it as one ruling: the words that FORCED line quotes (its MEANS and its ANSWER) are the quotes of the break, so do not DISAGREE because the LINK BROKEN line itself quotes no answer words; judge the break by those quoted words, under the rest of this rule (pkgECP, either side alike). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and a rival reading of a contested word is not a break when the answer quotes the row words that carry it (CARRIED BY: a verse the answering round cites, at least 6 words in a row); layers named without such words do not carry a rival reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; pkgECW; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. Its cure line is PRESSED: D<n> vs C<m> | [<round>] | <the pressing words in quotation marks>, the round [DR1] or [DR2] against the defender, [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3] against the challenger, its words standing word for word in that round; it does not cure when a later round of the side that holds the link names every pressed witness the line rests on. A FORCED line breaks a link by meaning only when its MEANS quotes the pressing side's own sentence in the round it names; a verse re-quoted as the MEANS is not that, and when the item carries a CODE CHECK saying so, DISAGREE (pkgEFG, either side alike). When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. THE FOOTING RULE (pkgECB, ASK 267; either side alike): a LINK BROKEN line whose ground is that the link's step has no footing, or that its footing is borrowed from its own side's contested links, is not a break by meaning, and the meaning test above does not decide it: that the answer's words can agree with the meaning pressed does not answer a missing footing. On such a line a fit that rests on the very step the line says has no footing, or on the answering side's own contested links, is not a fit. AGREE when the answering side's rounds give that step no footing but its own contested links; DISAGREE when you quote the answering side's own words, in the round that gives them, footing the step on rows that are not its own contested links. Footing is the side's own rows and chain, not one verse that states the step (DG-61): a line that only says no verse states the step rests on an absence. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds. CARRIED BY (pkgECW, either side alike): when you DISAGREE with RIGHT: STANDS because the answer's quoted words carry a meaning the link can agree with (a rival reading included), end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", a verse the answering round cites (any layer, the order rows included); or -- CARRIED BY: [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>) at <reference>, a word that verse holds. Without it the STANDS is recorded and not sent back. The CARRIED BY row is never the line's own pressed verse (a verse named at the head of the line, or the GROUND's [L1] verse; for a FORCED line, those of its collision line): that verse holds the words in dispute, and quoting it again shows no rival reading. Read the answer with every other verse either side quoted on the subject (Isaiah 28:10). A CARRIED BY on the pressed verse is recorded and not sent back (ASK 355). When you AGREE that a link is BROKEN, end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", the row whose words the rival reading cannot also hold (ASK 355, TRIAL: recorded only; the pressed-verse rule does not apply to an AGREE). A DISAGREE that rests on an absence, on THE WITNESS LEDGER, on THE FOOTING RULE, or on a line that quotes no answer words needs no CARRIED BY.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. An answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, its layers included (THE ANSWER IN FULL, when given under an ANSWER CHECK line); an opening grant followed by a layer that shows the fit is not a bare grant. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not. When the right grade is BROKEN and the answering side answered the pressed verse (an ANSWER CHECK line given you quotes its answer, graded MISSES or FAILS), the break is one of meaning and counts only as a FORCED line for the pair (ruling 421; the gate checks it, K-G4): your reason says so and names it, FORCED: <Dn vs Cm> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing sentence>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the answer's words>" -- FAILS: "<the words that cannot agree>". Never ask for a plain LINK BROKEN line on a witness the side answered (pkgEHF). CARRIED BY (pkgECW, ASK 346, either side alike): when you DISAGREE with RIGHT: UNDERDETERMINED, end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", the row the answering round cites that leaves the point open; or -- CARRIED BY: [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>) at <reference>, a word that verse holds. Without it the push is recorded and not sent back. The CARRIED BY row is never the line's own pressed verse (a verse named at the head of the line, or the GROUND's [L1] verse): that verse holds the words in dispute (Isaiah 28:10); a CARRIED BY on it is recorded and not sent back (ASK 355).
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. A ground that restates the defender's own words for the keystone, given to you under THE DEFENDER'S OWN WORDS FOR THE KEYSTONE (its opening statement, or its premise line for that link), rests on the debate's words: the defender's thesis restated is not the judge's own doctrine (pkgEKD). AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it. It is also UNEXHIBITED when the kept claim still takes the dropped limb as given (pkgNRW, ASK 272; either side alike): when the item gives a NARROWED line, test the kept claim, not the sentence that disowns the limb. If the kept claim holds only by taking the dropped limb as given, and the block's [L4] does not conclude the kept claim from its rows, your RIGHT is COUNTED; write (UNEXHIBITED: the kept claim takes as given <the dropped limb>, which its rows do not give and its [L4] does not reach), quoting the kept claim. If the block's [L4] reaches the kept claim from its rows without the dropped limb, your RIGHT is SPARED. A disowning sentence such as "the link does not rest on it" is not footing. This is not a demand for a stating verse (DG-61): it applies only to a kept claim that needs the limb its own side dropped.
RULE E-PREM, A RECOUNTED LINE (pkgERC). When a judge's line says the engine recounted it, that judge's ruling on premise N is the one its STORED COUNTED PREMISES give: COUNTED when N is listed, SPARED when it is not; the line's silence is not a SPARED ruling. Judge that ruling as any other, from the block, the judge's line before the recount and its own collision lines shown. When the ruling is COUNTED and none of those lines gives a ground for premise N, say "counted with no stated ground" in your sentence.
RULE E-PREM, THE COUNTED KIND (pkgEPS). UNEXHIBITED means a missing layer: the answering block does not exhibit a layer its footing needs. When your RIGHT is COUNTED, begin your sentence with its kind in brackets: (UNEXHIBITED: lacks [L1]), naming each layer ([L1], [L2] or [L3]) the block does not exhibit; or (CONCEDED), quoting the side's own words that give the premise up. A ground of fit or meaning (the answer does not meet a pressed verse, or reads it another way) is not a missing layer: it is graded at the collision (RULE E-COL, RULE E-HOLD), not counted here, so it is not COUNTED; except (ruling 372) when this judge's own ANSWER CHECK line, given you under its line, grades a witness pressed against this premise MISSES or FAILS: that witness is unanswered and the premise is COUNTED; write (UNEXHIBITED: <the verse> unanswered, ruling 372) (pkgP72). FOOTING BORROWED FROM CONTESTED LINKS (pkgBCL). A shown chain is footing only through its rows and what the other side has granted. When a step of premise N's [L4] takes as given the conclusion of the same side's own other links (it names them, as "(Links 1 to 3)"), and the other side has not granted that conclusion, that step is the disputed point itself and is not footing for premise N: your RIGHT is COUNTED; write (UNEXHIBITED: [L4] footing borrowed from contested Links <n>), quoting the step. This holds for a NARROWED premise too: narrowing the link does not make a borrowed step footing. This is not a missing-row charge (DG-61): it applies only to a step that rests on the side's own contested links. When that conclusion is granted, or the [L4] reaches premise N from its rows without the borrowed step, your RIGHT is SPARED.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
RULE E-B7 (a premise counted UNEXHIBITED while the same judge grades MEETS an answer on the same verse; ruling 421, one judge may not hold both on one ground). UNEXHIBITED says the side did not show the fact the premise assumes. MEETS says the side's answer showed how the verse fits its case against the press. Decide FIRST the right reading: SAME GROUND when a MEETS line's press (its MEANS) and its answer concern the very fact the premise is counted as missing, so the two rulings cannot both stand; DIFFERENT GROUND when the press concerns another fact than the one the premise assumes (for example, the press is about who is addressed, while the premise is about whose house she is of). Read only the premise entry, the judge's count and the ANSWER CHECK lines given you. RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. An opening grant ("I grant it") followed by a layer that shows how the verse fits the answering side's case MEETS. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not. A charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never VOID for its words (ruling 421).
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. A LINK BROKEN line given with THE SAME JUDGE'S FORCED LINE on that collision is read with it as one ruling: the words that FORCED line quotes (its MEANS and its ANSWER) are the quotes of the break, so do not DISAGREE because the LINK BROKEN line itself quotes no answer words; judge the break by those quoted words, under the rest of this rule (pkgECP, either side alike). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and a rival reading of a contested word is not a break when the answer quotes the row words that carry it (CARRIED BY: a verse the answering round cites, at least 6 words in a row); layers named without such words do not carry a rival reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; pkgECW; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. Its cure line is PRESSED: D<n> vs C<m> | [<round>] | <the pressing words in quotation marks>, the round [DR1] or [DR2] against the defender, [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3] against the challenger, its words standing word for word in that round; it does not cure when a later round of the side that holds the link names every pressed witness the line rests on. A FORCED line breaks a link by meaning only when its MEANS quotes the pressing side's own sentence in the round it names; a verse re-quoted as the MEANS is not that, and when the item carries a CODE CHECK saying so, DISAGREE (pkgEFG, either side alike). When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. THE FOOTING RULE (pkgECB, ASK 267; either side alike): a LINK BROKEN line whose ground is that the link's step has no footing, or that its footing is borrowed from its own side's contested links, is not a break by meaning, and the meaning test above does not decide it: that the answer's words can agree with the meaning pressed does not answer a missing footing. On such a line a fit that rests on the very step the line says has no footing, or on the answering side's own contested links, is not a fit. AGREE when the answering side's rounds give that step no footing but its own contested links; DISAGREE when you quote the answering side's own words, in the round that gives them, footing the step on rows that are not its own contested links. Footing is the side's own rows and chain, not one verse that states the step (DG-61): a line that only says no verse states the step rests on an absence. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds. CARRIED BY (pkgECW, either side alike): when you DISAGREE with RIGHT: STANDS because the answer's quoted words carry a meaning the link can agree with (a rival reading included), end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", a verse the answering round cites (any layer, the order rows included); or -- CARRIED BY: [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>) at <reference>, a word that verse holds. Without it the STANDS is recorded and not sent back. The CARRIED BY row is never the line's own pressed verse (a verse named at the head of the line, or the GROUND's [L1] verse; for a FORCED line, those of its collision line): that verse holds the words in dispute, and quoting it again shows no rival reading. Read the answer with every other verse either side quoted on the subject (Isaiah 28:10). A CARRIED BY on the pressed verse is recorded and not sent back (ASK 355). When you AGREE that a link is BROKEN, end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", the row whose words the rival reading cannot also hold (ASK 355, TRIAL: recorded only; the pressed-verse rule does not apply to an AGREE). A DISAGREE that rests on an absence, on THE WITNESS LEDGER, on THE FOOTING RULE, or on a line that quotes no answer words needs no CARRIED BY.

STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. An answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, its layers included (THE ANSWER IN FULL, when given under an ANSWER CHECK line); an opening grant followed by a layer that shows the fit is not a bare grant. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it. It is also UNEXHIBITED when the kept claim still takes the dropped limb as given (pkgNRW, ASK 272; either side alike): when the item gives a NARROWED line, test the kept claim, not the sentence that disowns the limb. If the kept claim holds only by taking the dropped limb as given, and the block's [L4] does not conclude the kept claim from its rows, your RIGHT is COUNTED; write (UNEXHIBITED: the kept claim takes as given <the dropped limb>, which its rows do not give and its [L4] does not reach), quoting the kept claim. If the block's [L4] reaches the kept claim from its rows without the dropped limb, your RIGHT is SPARED. A disowning sentence such as "the link does not rest on it" is not footing. This is not a demand for a stating verse (DG-61): it applies only to a kept claim that needs the limb its own side dropped.

When a judge's line says the engine recounted it, that judge's ruling on premise N is the one its STORED COUNTED PREMISES give: COUNTED when N is listed, SPARED when it is not; the line's silence is not a SPARED ruling. RULE E-B7 (a premise counted UNEXHIBITED while the same judge grades MEETS an answer on the same verse; ruling 421, one judge may not hold both on one ground). RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. An opening grant ("I grant it") followed by a layer that shows how the verse fits the answering side's case MEETS. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not. A charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never VOID for its words (ruling 421).
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. A LINK BROKEN line given with THE SAME JUDGE'S FORCED LINE on that collision is read with it as one ruling: the words that FORCED line quotes (its MEANS and its ANSWER) are the quotes of the break, so do not DISAGREE because the LINK BROKEN line itself quotes no answer words; judge the break by those quoted words, under the rest of this rule (pkgECP, either side alike). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and a rival reading of a contested word is not a break when the answer quotes the row words that carry it (CARRIED BY: a verse the answering round cites, at least 6 words in a row); layers named without such words do not carry a rival reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; pkgECW; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. Its cure line is PRESSED: D<n> vs C<m> | [<round>] | <the pressing words in quotation marks>, the round [DR1] or [DR2] against the defender, [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3] against the challenger, its words standing word for word in that round; it does not cure when a later round of the side that holds the link names every pressed witness the line rests on. A FORCED line breaks a link by meaning only when its MEANS quotes the pressing side's own sentence in the round it names; a verse re-quoted as the MEANS is not that, and when the item carries a CODE CHECK saying so, DISAGREE (pkgEFG, either side alike). When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. THE FOOTING RULE (pkgECB, ASK 267; either side alike): a LINK BROKEN line whose ground is that the link's step has no footing, or that its footing is borrowed from its own side's contested links, is not a break by meaning, and the meaning test above does not decide it: that the answer's words can agree with the meaning pressed does not answer a missing footing. On such a line a fit that rests on the very step the line says has no footing, or on the answering side's own contested links, is not a fit. AGREE when the answering side's rounds give that step no footing but its own contested links; DISAGREE when you quote the answering side's own words, in the round that gives them, footing the step on rows that are not its own contested links. Footing is the side's own rows and chain, not one verse that states the step (DG-61): a line that only says no verse states the step rests on an absence. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds. CARRIED BY (pkgECW, either side alike): when you DISAGREE with RIGHT: STANDS because the answer's quoted words carry a meaning the link can agree with (a rival reading included), end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", a verse the answering round cites (any layer, the order rows included); or -- CARRIED BY: [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>) at <reference>, a word that verse holds. Without it the STANDS is recorded and not sent back. The CARRIED BY row is never the line's own pressed verse (a verse named at the head of the line, or the GROUND's [L1] verse; for a FORCED line, those of its collision line): that verse holds the words in dispute, and quoting it again shows no rival reading. Read the answer with every other verse either side quoted on the subject (Isaiah 28:10). A CARRIED BY on the pressed verse is recorded and not sent back (ASK 355). When you AGREE that a link is BROKEN, end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", the row whose words the rival reading cannot also hold (ASK 355, TRIAL: recorded only; the pressed-verse rule does not apply to an AGREE). A DISAGREE that rests on an absence, on THE WITNESS LEDGER, on THE FOOTING RULE, or on a line that quotes no answer words needs no CARRIED BY.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. An answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, its layers included (THE ANSWER IN FULL, when given under an ANSWER CHECK line); an opening grant followed by a layer that shows the fit is not a bare grant. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not. When the right grade is BROKEN and the answering side answered the pressed verse (an ANSWER CHECK line given you quotes its answer, graded MISSES or FAILS), the break is one of meaning and counts only as a FORCED line for the pair (ruling 421; the gate checks it, K-G4): your reason says so and names it, FORCED: <Dn vs Cm> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing sentence>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the answer's words>" -- FAILS: "<the words that cannot agree>". Never ask for a plain LINK BROKEN line on a witness the side answered (pkgEHF). CARRIED BY (pkgECW, ASK 346, either side alike): when you DISAGREE with RIGHT: UNDERDETERMINED, end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", the row the answering round cites that leaves the point open; or -- CARRIED BY: [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>) at <reference>, a word that verse holds. RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. A ground that restates the defender's own words for the keystone, given to you under THE DEFENDER'S OWN WORDS FOR THE KEYSTONE (its opening statement, or its premise line for that link), rests on the debate's words: the defender's thesis restated is not the judge's own doctrine (pkgEKD). RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is also UNEXHIBITED when the kept claim still takes the dropped limb as given (pkgNRW, ASK 272; either side alike): when the item gives a NARROWED line, test the kept claim, not the sentence that disowns the limb. RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. An opening grant ("I grant it") followed by a layer that shows how the verse fits the answering side's case MEETS. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not. A charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never VOID for its words (ruling 421).
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. A LINK BROKEN line given with THE SAME JUDGE'S FORCED LINE on that collision is read with it as one ruling: the words that FORCED line quotes (its MEANS and its ANSWER) are the quotes of the break, so do not DISAGREE because the LINK BROKEN line itself quotes no answer words; judge the break by those quoted words, under the rest of this rule (pkgECP, either side alike). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and a rival reading of a contested word is not a break when the answer quotes the row words that carry it (CARRIED BY: a verse the answering round cites, at least 6 words in a row); layers named without such words do not carry a rival reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; pkgECW; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. Its cure line is PRESSED: D<n> vs C<m> | [<round>] | <the pressing words in quotation marks>, the round [DR1] or [DR2] against the defender, [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3] against the challenger, its words standing word for word in that round; it does not cure when a later round of the side that holds the link names every pressed witness the line rests on.
